meta.env: Autodesk Maya 2024 GUI (apiVersion 20240000, cutIdentifier 202302170737-4500172811, Qt 5.15.2) on Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 10.0.26100 x64; scene linear unit cm at rest; maya.exe pid 788; launched with -script (no commandPort); the launcher created one unsaved node before the driver ran
meta.purpose: Run the shipped maya_scene_module.py from the #273 branch on live Maya 2024 and compare its world boxes with cmds.exactWorldBoundingBox, then time the analysis path at 100 flat objects, 1000 flat objects and one 200-deep chain.
meta.verdict: The +30 parent / -30 child case reports the true 10 cube (the old cached-box read reports 18.66) and equals cmds.exactWorldBoundingBox; the four #266 cases still match; an empty mesh inside the measured group does not drag the union to the origin (a negative control without the filter does include it); the driver left the session open and its unsaved bystander in place; get_scene_graph took 10.21 ms at 115 objects, 106.23 ms at 1015 and 186.91 ms on one 200-deep chain (216 objects). The runs also caught three real-API facts the fake layer had wrong: MDagPath.child() returns an MObject, MBoundingBox has no isEmpty()/is_empty with a default box of min=max=(0,0,0), and MFnMesh refuses a mesh node with no geometry data (polyEvaluate is the vertex-count fallback).
meta.claim_boundary: Proves the mechanism and the timings on Maya 2024 on this box only. It does NOT prove Maya 2025/2026, and it does not exercise the MCP tool wrapper: the driver execs the shipped module source (sha256 in env.module_sha256). The 100/1000 scenes are flat (one shape per transform). The chain row is outside the object-count target: at depth 200 the walk is O(depth^2), so a pathological deep hierarchy can exceed 200 ms even though flat 1000-object scenes did not in these runs. Timing varies run to run on a GUI session; the spread is recorded under performance.timing_variance.

provenance.stub_divergence: tests/maya_stub represents an empty box as min=+inf/max=-inf; Maya 2024 reads 0..0 with no isEmpty(). Both make expand() work from the first point, and the product decides emptiness with its own 'measured' flag, but the stub cannot reproduce the real representation. A mesh is therefore classified by vertex count, not by its box alone.
provenance.scene_safety: Only triage273_-prefixed nodes were created and are deleted in a finally block; the launcher's triage273_bystander node is NOT deleted by the driver; currentUnit is restored; leftover is empty and restored_unit is cm; file(new=True) was never called.
